notes:
Account: PixelForge Assist — developer-first company building an IDE copilot embedded in their desktop editor and cloud CI. Primary ask: strict model/version pinning and reproducibility for code completions across releases.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-12: Intro call (Jordan). High-level product fit confirmed — want low-latency streaming completions and deterministic diffs when model changes.
- 2026-01-30: Technical deep-dive with Maya (SE) — discussed tokenization differences, quantization variance, seeding RNG for determinism. Fireflies: ff_2026-02-15_pf-assist-call-9821.

Use-case & requirements (short):
- Workload: IDE copilot + background CI linting (real-time completions + offline batch reranking).
- Latency target: <= 60ms median for inline completions; tail p95 <= 150ms for small snippets.
- Throughput: bursts up to 200 concurrent editors per region during peak releases.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for dedicated capacity if guarantees reproducible outputs.
- Model preferences: open weights acceptable; must support pinned model hashes and immutable model artifact ids.
- Routing/fallback: want canary -> ramp -> full rollout with automatic rollback on quality/regression gates.
- Reproducibility: deterministic completions for a given model pin + prompt seed; stable API behavior across minor infra updates; documented release notes for kernel/runtime changes.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logging for prompt/response retention, KMS integration for keys, EU data residency for some customers.

Evaluation plan / POC scope:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Inbound POC on Redwood Hosted with model pinning; run canonical evals to establish baseline metrics (perplexity, edit-distance, unit tests passing).
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Dedicated pool test with canary rollout (5% traffic) to validate deterministic outputs across redistributions and kernel changes. Capture drift metrics and byte-level diffs.
- Phase 3: Integrate rollback triggers (quality gates) connected to our eval harness. If failure rate > 3% or average edit-distance increases by > 1.5x, auto-scale back to previous model.

Questions from their engineering team (paraphrased):
- "How do you guarantee identical completions after a minor runtime optimization?"
- "Can we pin both model artifact hash and inference kernel version?"
- "What are the reproducibility SLAs and audit trail formattings?"

Notes from SE:
- Recommended: model artifact immutability + kernel-version label in rollout config; include checksum in SDK response headers for easy client verification.
- Suggest exposing deterministic seed control for offline CI runs; for streaming/editor UX, provide block-level replayable tokens.

Next immediate steps (short):
- Schedule security sync (infosec + Maya) week of 2026-03-08.
- Customer to supply final eval prompts and CI runner access (completed by 2026-03-10 ideally).
- Redwood to prepare POC canary runbook and pricing estimate for dedicated pool.
